title: Palamas and the uncreated light
hook: on Mount Athos, monks praying the Jesus Prayer say they see the light of Tabor

segments.voice: Yesterday, Dante's journey from a dark wood to heaven, and your line was the love that moves the sun.

Night on Mount Athos, a rocky peninsula in Greece, home to monks. In a small cell, a monk sits on a low stool, head bowed, breathing slowly. With each breath he says the same short prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me. Hours go by. And some of these monks say that in the stillness they see light. Not a lamp, not the moon: a light they say is God's own, the same light the disciples saw on Mount Tabor. Others laughed at them. Today's word is what the monks were doing.

Hesychasm. When Paul tells one church, in the King James Bible, to "study to be quiet," the Greek verb he uses is from the same family: hesychazo, to be still. Hesychasts are the people of stillness. Their prayer, the Jesus Prayer, grows out of cries in the Gospels: the tax collector's "God be merciful to me a sinner," and the blind man's "Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me." Said slowly, with the breath. And the light? They point to the Transfiguration. Jesus takes three disciples up a mountain, tradition says Tabor, and there, Matthew writes, "his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light." The monks say that light can still be seen. A learned man named Barlaam mocked them: God can't be seen with bodily eyes, so whatever you're seeing, it isn't God. A monk of Athos, Gregory Palamas, answered with a distinction. God's essence, what God is in himself, is beyond every creature, forever. But God's energies, his life, his grace, his light, are truly God too, uncreated, and God gives them. So a person can really share in God's light without swallowing up God's mystery. Church councils in Constantinople sided with Palamas, and Orthodox Christians honor him as a saint. Western churches have read his ideas in different ways, and theologians still discuss them. For the people of stillness, the quiet was never empty. It was a cell kept ready for light.
screen: `HAVE MERCY ON ME, WITH THE BREATH.`

segments.voice: If you can, dim the room and light a candle, a small lamp, or even a blank white screen, and let your eyes rest on it without staring hard, breathing slowly in and out. If you pray, you can say the old prayer of the monks with the breath, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me; if not, let the breath be the prayer and the light be enough.
Hesychasm. Stillness: a way of prayer from the Christian East, the Jesus Prayer said with the breath, defended by Gregory Palamas.
Your line: the light of tabor. Seven days, from Elizabeth's bread to a cell on Athos. A week closes: day eight hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: Orthodox Christians, and some Catholics and Protestants, pray the Jesus Prayer, often with a prayer rope, and Orthodox churches keep a Sunday in Lent in memory of Gregory Palamas.

chat.meaning: Hesychasts pray the Jesus Prayer slowly, with the breath, in stillness. It grows out of cries for mercy in the Gospels.

Mount Athos.meaning: a rocky peninsula in Greece, home to monks

Tabor.meaning: by tradition, the mountain of the Transfiguration

Transfiguration.meaning: when Jesus's face shone like the sun before three disciples

Barlaam.meaning: a learned man who mocked the monks' light

Gregory Palamas.meaning: a monk of Athos who defended the people of stillness

notes: 1 Thessalonians 4:11 'study to be quiet' renders ἡσυχάζειν; the script ties hesychasm to this verb family. Confirm under the claims rule (this is a word-root claim drawn from the cited verse's Greek).

Tabor as the mountain is tradition (the Gospels say 'an high mountain'); the script says 'tradition says Tabor'.
Barlaam's objection and Palamas's essence/energies distinction paraphrased; councils in Constantinople named without dates. Confirm the summary is fair to both Orthodox and Western readers.
